info.name: SMemories - media
info.description: Photo upload, list, download and delete (T-009, T-046), on the v2 contract since T-069 (`/api/media/create`, `/api/media/get-list`, `/api/media/get-content`, `/api/media/delete`; `{status,data}` envelope, `ERROR_*` codes, Unix ms timestamps; `get-content` is binary on success and the error envelope on failure). Accounts and yearbooks still use the v1 routes until their own tasks. Run from the postman/ directory (newman run media.postman_collection.json --working-dir .) against an API started with SMEM_ENV=dev and a reachable MinIO (make up). Each run registers 2 users (limit 5 per hour per IP; run `make reset-limits` or raise SMEM_RATE_REGISTER_PER_HOUR before a third run in the hour). Run the whole collection in order: Edge cases reuses the two users of the Full flow. Not covered here because a collection cannot generate files: the 11 MiB size cap (413), quotas and the upload rate limit; the Go integration tests cover them.

item.name: Full flow

exec: // Runs before every request in the folder; generate only before the first one so the whole flow shares one pair of accounts.

item.name: 1. Register user A
2. Register user B
3. A creates a yearbook
4. A uploads a JPEG with GPS EXIF and orientation 6 (200x100 becomes 100x200)

exec: pm.test('created_at is Unix ms, content type from the server', () => { pm.expect(m.created_at).to.be.above(1.7e12); pm.expect(m.content_type).to.eql('image/jpeg'); pm.expect(m.yearbook_id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('bookId')); });

item.name: 5. A downloads the display version: right headers, no EXIF/GPS left
6. A downloads the thumbnail
6b. A downloads the print size (1800 px long edge)
6c. A uploads a 2400x1200 JPEG (larger than the 1800 px print size)
6d. A downloads the print size of the large photo: long edge exactly 1800 px
6e. A deletes the large photo (keeps the later list steps unchanged)
7. A fetches a byte range
7b. HEAD answers the headers and no body
8. A sets the cover and the profile photo
9. A sets the profile photo
10. B cannot read A's photo
11. B deleting A's photo answers 200 but deletes nothing
12. A can still read it
13. A deletes the photo
14. Deleting again is idempotent
15. The photo is gone

exec: pm.test('the error is uncacheable JSON, never an image', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Cache-Control')).to.eql('no-store'); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type')).to.match(/^application\/json/); pm.expect(pm.response.json().request_id).to.be.a('string'); });

item.name: 16. The cover and profile photo were cleared
17. A uploads a PNG with transparency (stays PNG)
18. The PNG is served as image/png
19. A uploads a second photo
20. A lists with limit=1: the newest photo first, and a cursor

exec: pm.test('item shape: no storage keys, hashes or URLs', () => { pm.expect(m).to.have.all.keys('id','yearbook_id','content_type','bytes','width','height','created_at'); pm.expect(m.yearbook_id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('bookId')); pm.expect(m.created_at).to.be.a('number'); pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/object_key|thumb_key|sha256|yearbooks\//); });

item.name: 21. A pages with the cursor: the older photo, no next cursor
22. A lists with the defaults: both photos, newest first
23. uploader=contributor lists nothing yet

exec: pm.test('empty array, not null', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.eql({status: 'OK', data: {items: [], next_id: ''}}));

item.name: 24. uploader=all lists both
25. A deletes the photo the cursor points at
26. The old cursor still works: the older photo

exec: pm.test('the older photo, nothing skipped or repeated', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.items.map(m => m.id)).to.eql([pm.collectionVariables.get('mediaId2')]); pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.next_id).to.eql(''); });

item.name: 27. A deletes the yearbook (its photos go with it)
28. The photo of the deleted yearbook is gone
Edge cases
E1. A creates a yearbook
E2. B creates a yearbook
E3. B uploads a photo to B's book (used below)
E4. Upload without a session - 401
E5. Upload to someone else's yearbook - 404
E6. Upload to an unknown yearbook - 404
E7. Upload from a foreign origin - 403
E8. HTML renamed to .jpg - 415
E9. GIF - 415
E10. Empty file - 415
E11. PNG whose header claims 60000x60000 pixels - 400
E12. JSON body instead of multipart - 415
E13. Multipart without a file part - 400
E13b. Upload without yearbook_id - 400
E14. File sent under the wrong field name - 400
E15. Download with an unknown size - 400
E15b. Download without id - 400
E16. Download without a session - 401
E17. A cannot read B's photo - 404
E18. A cannot use B's photo as a cover - 400
E19. A cannot use B's photo as a profile photo - 400
E20. Unknown media id as cover - 400
E21. Deleting an unknown media id - 200 (idempotent)
E21b. Delete without id - 400
E22. Delete without a session - 401
E23. List without a session - 401
E24. B lists A's yearbook - 404
E25. A lists B's yearbook - 404
E26. List an unknown yearbook - 404
E27. List with limit=0 - 400 ERROR_PARAM
E28. List with limit=-1 - 400 ERROR_PARAM
E29. List with limit=101 - 400 ERROR_PARAM
E30. List with limit=abc - 400 ERROR_PARAM
E31. List with uploader=everyone - 400 ERROR_PARAM
E32. List with next_id=!!! - 400 ERROR_PARAM
E33. List with next_id=YWJj - 400 ERROR_PARAM
E34. An old-style plain-number next_id (MQ) is refused - 400
E35. B lists its own yearbook: only B's photo
E36. A's next_id on B's yearbook is refused - 400 (a token is bound to its yearbook)
E36b. A tampered next_id is refused - 400
E37. Clean up: A deletes the yearbook
E38. Clean up: B deletes the yearbook
